findings.title: Computed Zod keys do not validate or preserve token expiry fields
findings.body: Using a Zod schema's toString() as an object key produces a literal key such as "[object Object]", not a dynamic property validator. The two computed keys also collide. Since z.object strips unknown properties, synced responses lose expires_in, expiry_date, and refresh_token instead of preserving them. Consumers such as Zoom then calculate expiry from undefined and cannot persist usable credentials. Define explicit supported fields or a passthrough schema with appropriate expiry validation.

findings.title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a placeholder
findings.body: This helper assigns the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the parsed response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office 365 permits refresh_token to be absent and previously retained the existing token when merging the response. The new placeholder overwrites that valid token in the database, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

findings.title: Persist the parsed token data rather than the safeParse result
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the credentials themselves. Saving this wrapper as credential.key removes access_token and refresh_token from the expected top-level location. After any Google token refresh, even with syncing disabled, subsequent service construction fails googleCredentialSchema validation.

findings.title: Normalize the sync response for SDK and Axios callers
findings.body: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but the fallback branch returns whatever the provider callback returns. Google and the Zoho integrations read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly from an SDK token object. None of those properties exist on a fetch Response, regardless of the JSON returned by the sync endpoint. Enabling syncing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Parse and normalize the response or adapt each caller to the sync response contract.

findings.title: Pass the user ID rather than the credential ID to token syncing
findings.body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is a Cal.com user ID, but Bigin passes credentialId. The helper sends that value as calcomUserId to the parent platform, requesting tokens for the wrong user whenever these IDs differ. This can fail refreshes or associate another user's tokens with this credential. Carry credential.userId through to this call; team credentials should retain the provider fallback.

findings.title: Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce refresh
findings.body: The new getClient implementation calls prisma.credential.update, but this file does not import or declare prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and throws ReferenceError at runtime after a successful token request, preventing Salesforce client initialization and event operations.

findings.title: Use the installed Zoom app slug in sync requests
findings.body: The refresh request sends appSlug "zoomvideo", but Zoom credentials and the callback use the app ID/slug "zoom". A parent app store resolving the supplied appSlug against the same slugs used by the credential webhook cannot find this integration. Send "zoom" so refresh and credential creation identify the same app.
